quests.question: The curriculum was redesigned ___ students would graduate with practical skills.
quests.hint: This phrase signals an intended purpose — a more formal version of 'so that'.
quests.explanation: 'In order that' introduces a purpose in formal writing — the redesign was intended to build practical skills.

quests.question: Traditional exams test memorization, ___ project-based assessment tests applied understanding.
quests.hint: Two assessment methods are being placed side by side in contrast.
quests.explanation: 'While' can contrast two related facts — two methods measuring two different skills.

quests.question: The scholarship helps students ___ it covers tuition, though not housing costs.
quests.hint: This introduces the exact respect in which the scholarship helps, not simply why.
quests.explanation: 'In that' specifies the exact respect in which something is true — covering tuition is precisely how it helps.

quests.question: ___ earlier students start learning a language, ___ easier it becomes for them.
quests.hint: This links two increasing degrees together, step for step.
quests.explanation: 'The...the' shows that one change causes a matching change — starting earlier leads to greater ease.

quests.question: ___ class sizes have grown significantly, the school hired three new teachers.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for a staffing decision.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for a decision — larger classes justify the new hires.

quests.question: The textbook is outdated, ___ the teacher supplements it with current examples.
quests.hint: A flaw is compensated for by an additional effort.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — an outdated textbook is offset by the teacher's extra material.

quests.question: ___ remote candidates performed just as well in interviews, the company dropped its location requirement.
quests.hint: This phrase introduces an observed fact as the basis for a policy change.
quests.explanation: 'Seeing that' introduces an observed fact as the basis for a decision — equal performance led to dropping the requirement.

quests.question: Junior staff receive close supervision, ___ senior staff are trusted to work independently.
quests.hint: Two staff levels are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two levels of staff with two different degrees of supervision.

quests.question: The proposal was approved quickly ___ it had unanimous support from every department.
quests.hint: Full agreement explains the quick approval.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a result — unanimous support caused the fast approval.

quests.question: The new contract benefits freelancers ___ it guarantees payment within fourteen days.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the benefit extends.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the benefit is limited to this specific guarantee.

quests.question: The handbook was translated into five languages ___ every employee could understand company policy.
quests.hint: This formal phrase introduces a purpose, like 'so that', in more official writing.
quests.explanation: 'In order that' introduces a purpose in formal writing — the translation was intended to make policy accessible to everyone.

quests.question: The new hire is not only highly skilled ___ also remarkably easy to work with.
quests.hint: 'Not only' always pairs with one word to add a second impressive quality.
quests.explanation: 'Not only...but also' adds a second impressive quality to the first — skill and being easy to work with.

quests.question: Domestic flights rarely require advance check-in, ___ international flights almost always do.
quests.hint: Two types of flights are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two flight types with two different check-in rules.

quests.question: The new visa policy helps business travelers ___ it removes the need for an in-person interview.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the policy's benefit extends.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the benefit for travelers is limited to this specific change.

quests.question: ___ fuel costs have risen sharply, several airlines have added a surcharge.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for a pricing decision.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for a decision — rising fuel costs justify the surcharge.

quests.question: The director filmed the scene ___ the actors were completely unaware of the camera.
quests.hint: This introduces a comparison to something that may not be true, in a formal tone.
quests.explanation: 'As though' introduces a comparison to an imagined situation, similar to 'as if' — the filming style suggested unawareness that may not have been real.

quests.question: Streaming services release entire seasons at once, ___ broadcast television airs one episode per week.
quests.hint: Two release formats are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two very different release schedules.

quests.question: Viewership dropped sharply after the format change, ___ producers reversed the decision.
quests.hint: A drop in viewers directly caused a reversal.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result — falling viewership caused producers to change course.

quests.question: Public consultations were extended ___ residents would have more time to respond.
quests.hint: Similar to 'so that' but more formal, this phrase introduces an intended purpose.
quests.explanation: 'In order that' introduces a purpose in formal writing — the extension was intended to give residents more time.

quests.question: ___ public transport use had fallen, the city reduced bus fares for a trial period.
quests.hint: This phrase introduces an observed fact as the basis for a decision.
quests.explanation: 'Seeing that' introduces an observed fact as the basis for a decision — falling ridership led to the trial fare reduction.

quests.question: Residents will vote on ___ the old theater should be restored ___ demolished.
quests.hint: Two possible outcomes are both on the ballot.
quests.explanation: 'Whether...or' introduces two possible outcomes under consideration — restoring the theater or demolishing it.

quests.question: The partnership works well ___ both companies share the same long-term goals.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the partnership's success depends.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the partnership's success is limited to this shared condition.

quests.question: The first draft focused on facts, ___ the final version balanced facts with clear analysis.
quests.hint: Two versions of the same document are being placed side by side in contrast.
quests.explanation: 'While' can contrast two related facts — two drafts with two different areas of focus.

quests.question: The report gained credibility ___ it was reviewed by three independent experts.
quests.hint: Independent review explains the credibility.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a result — expert review caused the report to gain credibility.

quests.question: ___ the pilot program succeeded, the city plans to expand it citywide.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for an expansion decision.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for a decision — the pilot's success justifies expanding it.

quests.question: The instructions were simplified ___ new users would need less training.
quests.hint: This is the formal, official-writing equivalent of 'so that'.
quests.explanation: 'In order that' introduces a purpose in formal writing — the simplified instructions were intended to reduce training time.

quests.question: Demand was ___ a surprise that the store had to reorder stock within a week.
quests.hint: This word takes a full noun phrase, not just a bare adjective, before 'that'.
quests.explanation: 'Such' combines with a noun phrase before 'that' — the surprising demand explains the quick reorder.

quests.question: The pilot phase relied on volunteers, ___ the full rollout will involve paid staff.
quests.hint: Two phases of the same project are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two phases run in two different ways.

quests.question: The forecast is reliable ___ conditions don't change drastically in the next few days.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the forecast's reliability extends, like 'insofar as'.
quests.explanation: 'To the extent that' means the same as 'insofar as' — the forecast's reliability depends on this specific condition holding.

quests.question: ___ the update improves performance ___ not, users will notice the new design immediately.
quests.hint: Two possible outcomes together form the subject of the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Whether...or' can start a sentence as its subject — either outcome, the new design will be immediately noticeable.
